title: Artifact for: Budgeting Dimensions in Multi-Relation Vector Indexes: Measure, Configure, Don't Predict
description: Measurement grids, fitted parameters, deployment measurements and analysis scripts for a study of dimension budgets in multi-relation vector indexes: given one PCA basis and several relevance relations, how many dimensions does each relation need, and when is a second graph worth its bytes. Contains 19 cells x 23-31 ranks of mAP@10 (486 rows), 38 cells x 18-31 ranks of recall@10 (1,126 rows), the eigenvalues and eta^2 per (encoder, corpus), every aggregate quoted in the paper, a sensitivity sweep over all 688 admissible two-point placements (253 rank pairs + 435 rho-target pairs, 13,072 evaluations), HNSW deployment measurements on three corpora (In-shop, INSTRE, Amazon reviews) including single-thread p50 latency and retention, a three-relation deployment, the cross-cell byte margin over the 90%-variance rule on 11 encoder-corpus pairs, a projection trained on the relation against the PCA prefix, a synthetic control that reproduces the central phenomenon without any third-party data, and 105 Python scripts plus 12 shell drivers. `bash repro.sh` regenerates the eleven tables that are a function of the released JSON, and a run leaves the working tree unchanged -- that is the claim the deposit makes. It needs only Python and numpy. The scripts that re-measure from raw corpora (sb_*.py) additionally need the corpora and embedding caches, which are not redistributed; README section 4 gives the order to run them in.
notes: Code (scripts/) is CC BY 4.0; measured data, tables and figures are CC BY-NC 4.0 because the DeepFashion release agreement restricts derived data to non-commercial use. Data files contain derived measurements only (curves, eigenvalues, fitted parameters). No images and no embeddings are redistributed; see LICENSE_NOTE.md.
